messages:
Emma (CS): Quick heads-up on Quellix onboarding — seeing higher than expected token cost and a bad tail on chat. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~730ms. Renewal call in 3 weeks, they asked for cost wins. Suggest a staged plan: int8 quant swap for non-critical traffic + routing split for realtime vs batch. Thoughts?

Andre (Solutions): +1. Customer explicitly asked for a 20-30% cost reduction. They can accept a slight drop in output fidelity for background tasks.

Leo (ML Eng): We can do int8 on their current variant (redwood-open-7b-v2). Expect ~28% cost drop and ~10-30ms extra latency vs fp16 depending on seq len. Need to run their eval set to check quality delta. Recommend canary: 5% -> 25% -> full if metrics pass.

Sam (SRE): Routing idea: route short, realtime requests to high-perf pool and everything else to quantized pool. That should keep user-facing latency tight while shifting volume. I can add a router policy.

Sam (SRE): Example policy snippet to start from:
```yaml
route:
  - match: "realtime == true and prompt_len < 512"
    pool: "gpu-low-latency"
    weight: 80
  - match: "default"
    pool: "quantized-cost"
    weight: 20
canary:
  percent: 5
  duration: 2h
```

Emma (CS): I'll pull their eval prompts and coordinate. @Leo can you run a quality check on 500 example prompts? Target: <=2% top-1 accuracy delta and p95 latency <= 800ms.

Quellix Admin: Sending the csv of 500 prompts to Emma now. We're keen to see cost numbers and won't block the canary if quality looks close.

OpsBot: Deploy plan created: canary-id=cq-1795554321, scheduled to start in 30m. Monitor: cost_per_token, p95_latency, quality_delta. Alerts set for quality_delta > 2% or p95 > 850ms.

Leo (ML Eng): Got the prompts, will run eval and post results here by EOD tomorrow. Also: recommend adding prefix caching for repeated templates — could shave another ~10% off cost.

Andre (Solutions): I'll draft a short customer note showing expected savings and fallback behavior for the renewal meeting.

Emma (CS): Next steps: 1) Leo runs eval (T+1d), 2) Sam deploys routing rule and canary (T+2d), 3) Andre prepares customer-facing summary (T+2d). I'll sync with renewal lead. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Quellix Admin: Thanks team — appreciate the proactive plan. We'll be available for quick follow-ups during the canary.
